name: antiphony
description: Antiphony — open, AT-Protocol-shaped call-and-response audio infrastructure: a headless API for storing, serving and enriching audio posts.

scripts.build: npm run build -w @antiphony/shared && npm run build -w @antiphony/capture-kit && npm run build -w @antiphony/core-api && npm run build -w @antiphony/audio-rendition
scripts.//dev: Runs core-api on the Workers runtime against local bindings. Put DATABASE_URL in apps/core-api/.dev.vars (gitignored) first — the database is a Worker secret, not a Hyperdrive binding.
scripts.test: npm run test --workspaces --if-present && npm run test:eslint-rules && npm run test:lexicons && npm run test:dependency-ranges && npm run test:design-tokens
scripts.//test:design-tokens: Asserts that all CSS and Astro source files strictly use design system tokens (--ap-*) with zero un-tokenized raw color codes leaking into production.
scripts.//test:eslint-rules: The custom ESLint rules' RuleTester suites use node:test, not vitest, so `--workspaces` never reaches them. The glob is quoted because bare `node --test eslint-rules/` also picks up the rule sources and exits non-zero.
scripts.//test:lexicons: Validates lexicons/ against upstream's encoding of the Lexicon spec (@atproto/lex-document), so an upstream spec change fails CI. Refs into app.bsky.*/com.atproto.* are reported, not resolved (see specs/xrpc-and-atproto-lex-strategy.md §7). Lives at the root because lexicons/ belongs to no workspace.
scripts.//test:dependency-ranges: Asserts every declared range is satisfied by the version package-lock.json resolves. Not redundant with `npm ci`: npm checks package.json against the lockfile's per-workspace manifest mirror, not the resolved tree, so a nested resolution can violate a declared range while `npm install` and `npm ci` both exit 0.
scripts.//knip: `--treat-config-hints-as-errors` is load-bearing: knip exits 0 on configuration hints (an `entry` pattern matching nothing, a redundant `ignore`), so without it config rot passes CI.

//allowScripts: npm 12+ runs a dependency's install script only if it is listed here (npm 10/11 ignore this field). esbuild fetches its platform binary (core-api cannot bundle without it); sharp backs Astro's image service in the docs build; fsevents is macOS-only. Entries are unpinned by name so a version bump does not re-block them. Add one with `npm install-scripts approve <pkg>`. npm 12 blocking workerd's postinstall is harmless: its binary arrives through a platform-specific optional dependency.
//devDependencies.semver: Declared because scripts/check-dependency-ranges.mjs imports it; relying on a transitive hoist breaks when the declaring package drops it. knip reports it as unlisted if removed.
//devDependencies.wrangler: Declared at the root because deploy-docs.yml runs `npx wrangler deploy` from the repo root. Without it the command relies on core-api's copy hoisting, and on a miss `npx` silently downloads the newest wrangler onto the deploy path. Keep in step with apps/core-api/package.json.
//devDependencies.zod: Declared at the root to force npm to hoist a single instance of zod across the monorepo. Without this, packages/shared and apps/core-api receive separate nested copies of zod in their node_modules, breaking @hono/zod-openapi's prototype schema extension.
//packageManager: The single source for the npm version: every workflow reads this field and installs it explicitly, because actions/setup-node does not switch npm on it. apps/audio-rendition/Dockerfile pins the same version by hand — keep the two in step. npm 10 and 12 install different trees from the same lockfile (12 honours `allowScripts`), so bump it deliberately.
//engines: Keep at or above the highest Node floor any dependency declares (jsdom 30 requires ^22.22.2). npm only warns on `engines` without engine-strict, so a stale floor shows up as a confusing install elsewhere; check `npm ls` warnings after a bump.
